description_paragraphs: This crime caper comedy mixes upbeat wit with deliciously dark humor, a difficult balance achieved with aplomb. British gangster George Thomason and his accomplice Ken team up with a pair of arrogant Americans for a massive diamond heist. When the theft goes sideways, George ends up on trial while his fellow thieves try to hunt down the hidden stash. Their plan involves sending American grifter Wanda to seduce George's stuffy lawyer Archie Leech, hoping to discover where George hid the loot. But Archie is bored with family and job and may be a more willing accomplice than Wanda suspected, especially when the chemistry between them is more than just a con job. A Fish Called Wanda is a smart and silly crowd pleaser. Winner of many accolades including an Oscar for Kevin Kline's role as a dispicable thief, the film rests on many "best of" lists, and is mong Central Cinema staff member Doug's favorite movies.

description_paragraphs: Thanks to an untimely demise via drowning, a young couple end up as poltergeists in their New England farmhouse, where they fail to meet the challenge of scaring away the insufferable new owners, who want to make drastic changes. In desperation, the undead newlyweds turn to an expert frightmeister, but he's got a diabolical agenda of his own. Beetlejuice gave director Burton the chance to unleash his visual style on the big screen. Iconis performances abound from the talented cast, including the great Catherine O'Hara as Delia Deetz.

description_paragraphs: Throughout his life Edward Bloom has always been a man of big appetites, enormous passions and tall tales. In his later years, he remains a huge mystery to his son, William. Now, to get to know the real man, Will begins piecing together a true picture of his father from flashbacks of his amazing adventures. Central Cinema staff memeber Zoe embraces Big Fish as "imagination come to life." Tim Burton's love of besplendid visuals and offbeat misfits plays perfectly into the story of a storyteller who's truths may or may not be rooted in reality. It's a great September Staff Pick for the big screen.

description_paragraphs: Debate the cinematic value of superhero movies all you want, but the first successful Marvel adaptation holds up as a relentlessly entertaining example of how to make a movie from a comic book source. Wesley Snipes is Blade, a bad-ass half-vampire on a mission to destroy the murderous bloodsuckers of the night. But the hunter becomes the hunted when forward thinking vampire Deacon Frost realizes that the sunproof Blade may be the key to resurrecting an ancient blood god. Snipes brings a lot to the role thanks to his extensive martial arts training and swordsmanship, as well as his natural charisma. Stephen Dorff almost steals the show as the villaneous Deacon Frost. Definitely a film worthy of a trip to big screen.

description_paragraphs: The rock'n'roll drag duo Camp Napalm is back at Central Cinema, presenting the most iconic erotic thriller of the early 90s. Catherine, a novelist with an insatiable sexual appetite, becomes a prime suspect when her boyfriend is brutally murdered in a fashion similar to a crime described in her latest story. San Francisco homicide detective Nick Curran is on the case, but starts to think Catherine probably didn't do it. Probably. At least he's sure enough to get sexually involved with Catherine and not feel bad about it. Except, what if his decision making skills are compromised by his attraction to Catherine? Given his history of making extremely poor professional choices, he's not sure what he's getting himself into, and Catherine may not let him get out of it alive. Sharon Stone instantly became a household name thanks to her role as the provacative suspect Catherine, who is clearly the smartest person in any room she honors with her presence; she'll make you have feelings. Thankfully Camp Napalm will be on hand to help you process these feelings and rock your night with their live performances.

description_paragraphs: Do you love movies and want to find others who can talk endlessly about them? Come join Cinemancy! Each month, a new movie is carefully selected. After the film the audience gathers to discuss themes, characters, plot, and symbolism. Hosted by Isabella Price. The Elephant Man John Merrick, a man with a range of disfigurements due to a rare congenital disorder, is exploited by traveling sideshows and treated as a freak. He is mistreated and dehumanized until a caring surgeon discovers him and takes him in. Soon, John is the toast of London, developing a strong sense of dignity and self-respect. With his second movie, David Lynch showed himself to be a multi-talented director, capable of intimate storytelling to deliver a greater message.

description_paragraphs: The classic Universal horror hit attacks the screen at Central Cinema. Dr. Henry Frankenstein obsesses over creating life. He's so obsessed that he assembles a creature from body parts of the dead. He and his assistant Fritz then bring the being to life; great success! Except, oops, the creature escapes and wreaks havoc (both accidentally and on purpose) on the nearby countryside. Based on Mary Shelly's sci-fi horror classic, Universal took the creature from her book and made him an icon. Boris Karloff's work as the creature holds up as one of horror's most remembered performances. Director James Whale delivers an audience pleasing tale that doesn't shy from the moral questions the book raises

description_paragraphs: Meet Jerry Dandrige. He's sweet, handsome, and likes to sleep in late. You might think he's the perfect neighbor. But before inviting Jerry in for a nightcap, there's one thing you should know: Jerry's drink of choice is warm, red, and straight from the jugular! Only 17-year-old Charley Brewster knows his neighbor's bloodcurdling secret. When Charley can't get anyone to believe him, he turns to TV horror host Peter Vincent who at one point was the "Great Vampire Killer of the movies. But Jerry gets wise to the duo's intentions, and sets his sights on those Charley holds dearest. Fright Night is a beloved 80's horror comedy for good reason, with as many laughs as frights on screen making for a fun flick to see on an October night.

description_paragraphs: After assassin Martin Blank has trouble focusing on his work, reulting in a failed assignment, he returns to his homestown of Grosse Point, Michigan, for his 10-year high school reunion. There he reconnects with Debi, his ex-girlfriend whom he jilted on prom night. Meanwhile, work gets in the way of his personal time when a Grosse Point local becomes a possible target, and a rival hitman rolls into town. Smart, funny, and sporting a fantastic soundtrack, Grosse Point Blank is among John Cusack's finest comedies and a great example oh how to make an upbeat rom-com with a twisted sense of humor.

description_paragraphs: It's time for the Baron's annual screening of what is perhaps the weirdest wildest sequels 80's horror has to offer. When a novelty-toy salesman is attacked by a deadly crew of men in suits, his doctor and his daughter hit the road to uncover a plot that goes massively over the top. Honestly, this film is never under the top. Only over. Just when you think no more weird things can happen...well, you get the idea. This is the rogue 1982 sequel that does its own thing. Thankfully, Baron Von Terror will be there to unpack our journey together, and trust us, there is a LOT to unpack.

description_paragraphs:
THESE BEAVERS DON’T QUIT!
While the good folx at The Grand Illusion Cinema locate a new home, they’ll host their monthly Hundreds of Beavers screenings at Central Cinema.
In this 19th century, supernatural winter epic, a drunken applejack salesman must go from zero to hero and become North America’s greatest fur trapper by defeating hundreds of beavers.
Created by Mike Cheslik and Ryland Brickson Cole Tews, the duo behind the modern cult hit LAKE MICHIGAN MONSTER (2018).

Presented in the original Telegu with English subtitles.

description_paragraphs: Another fine entry in the "Shakespear set in high school" subset of films hits our screen, thanks to September's Staff Picks. Viola Hastings is in a real jam, but is it really her fault? Okay, maybe pretending to be her twin brother Sebastian so she can play soccer at an exclusive boarding school isn't the most thought out plan. It is probably also a bad idea to start crushing on her roommate, especially if he's in love with someone else. Oh, and that someone else is Olivia, who starts falling for Sebastian, who is actually Viola in disguise. description_paragraphs: Legendary marshal Wyatt Earp, now a weary gunfighter, joins his brothers Morgan and Virgil to pursue their collective fortune in the thriving mining town of Tombstone. But Earp is forced to don a badge again and get help from his notorious pal Doc Holliday when a gang of renegade brigands and rustlers begins terrorizing the town. Tombstone overcame some serious behind-the-scenes turmoil to become one of the most memorable movies from the early 90s. Val Kilmer gives what may be his best performance as Doc Holliday, with quotable lines delivered flawlessly from beneath his amazing mustache. Central Cinema staff member Jeremy submitted this Staff Pick with the perfect review of this audience pleasing western: "Who doesn't love Tombstone?"
